Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted→Reserved: sizing proposal & proposed swap-out windows for NovaHealth

Hi Alice / Sanjay —

Great to reconnect after last week's call. Per our conversation I pulled together an initial reserved-capacity proposal so we can scope the Dedicated migration (hosted→reserved fleet) and lock a swap-out window that aligns with your release cadence. High level:

- Current hosted peak: ~2.4k qps inference requests (95th percentile) with avg prompt+resp ~420 tokens
- Target latency SLO: p95 < 120ms (production)
- Expected steady growth: +15% Q over Q across next 12 months

Preliminary sizing (attached: novahealth_sizing_v3.xlsx):
- 8x A100-80GB equiv for baseline steady-state (autoscale to 12 for peak bursts)
- Batching policy: target 16–32 token-batch windows guided by latency SLO
- KV cache warmup plan: prefilling for top 1k prefixes to avoid initial cold-start overhead

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal validation run with sample replay logs (we'll use a 48h window from your Nucleus export) — action: Rafael -> Aditya to run on staging reserved pool
2) Confirm cutover windows: tentative swap-out dates Mar 8–9 (low-traffic overnight UTC) or Mar 22–23 as fallback
3) Contract/procurement alignment: Mar 1 target signature to hit March capacity commit

Can you confirm: (a) whether the 48h logs are available for Aditya to run, and (b) if the Mar 8 window is feasible for your ops team?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Rafael

Folks — validation run complete (attached log: validation_run_0217.log). Summary:

- Validation config: 48h replay from NovaHealth logs, staging cluster: 8x A100-80GB equiv baseline + autoscale policy to 12x for 95th percentile bursts.
- Results: p50=42ms, p95=108ms (meets 120ms SLO at current load), sustained throughput cap ≈ 2.9k qps before queuing rises.
- GPU utilization: baseline 62% avg, bursts up to 88% at 95th percentile; KV cache hit after warmup reduced token compute by ≈ 12%
- Observations: initial warmup (first 30 minutes of trace) shows higher tail latency; recommend a scheduled cache prefilling job 12–24 hours before swap to pre-warm common prefixes.
- Risk notes: in the rare scenarios with long-context prompts (>1k tokens), p95 can spike ~40% — see section 4 of the log for timing breakdowns.

Recommended changes to proposal:
- Keep 8 GPUs baseline but set soft autoscale to 13 (one additional warm spare) for the first 14 days post-swap to absorb unexpected burst patterns.
- Add a pre-swap traffic mirroring window (2 hours) where we route 10% of production traffic to the reserved pool for sanity checks.

I'll attach the raw validation log and a short CSV with per-minute metrics. Let me know if you want me to run a longer 7-day replay.

-Aditya

Alice —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sending logs. Internal validation passed and Aditya recommends a small tweak: baseline 8 GPUs with a soft autoscale to 13 for the first two weeks and a 2-hour 10% traffic mirror prior to cutover. Marissa has drafted the swap runbook (attached in thread) and Grace confirmed pricing/proration notes.

Proposed operational plan (concise):
- Mar 8 23:00 UTC: start pre-swap priming and 2-hour 10% mirror to reserved pool
- Mar 9 01:15 UTC: health checks complete -> full traffic flip to reserved (30-min canary, 3-step rollout)
- Mar 9 03:00 UTC: monitor 24h for regressions; soft autoscale to 13 enabled for 14 days
- Rollback window: full rollback plan if p95 latency > 180ms for >10 minutes OR generation quality regression exceeds threshold in our eval suite

If this looks good, I'll send the DocuSign and propose Mar 1 signature to lock reserved commit. Attached: novahealth_sizing_v3.xlsx (final), validation_run_0217.log.

Rafael
